claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast, bulk polycrystalline MnNiSi-based alloy.
HPT followed by controlled low-temperature annealing will enhance the alloy's mechanical strength.
HPT followed by controlled low-temperature annealing will enhance the alloy's fracture toughness.
The proposed processing route will retain isothermal entropy change within 10% of the as-cast baseline value.
Room-temperature HPT at approximately 6 GPa for about five rotations will refine the grains of the MnNiSi-based alloy.
Annealing at 350°C for 30 minutes after HPT will reduce deformation-induced internal stresses.
Annealing at 350°C for 30 minutes will preserve an ultrafine-grained structure.
Controlled HPT and annealing will produce coherent and rearranged grain boundaries.
Grain refinement will increase yield strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Grain refinement will increase toughness through the Hall–Petch effect.
Post-HPT annealing will preserve magnetic-domain configurations that facilitate a large magnetocaloric effect.
The processed alloy will have significantly greater mechanical strength than the as-cast baseline.
The processed alloy will have significantly greater fracture toughness than the as-cast baseline.
Excessive grain refinement or defect introduction outside the proposed processing window could compromise magnetic performance.
The precise HPT and annealing window needed to balance mechanical and magnetocaloric performance is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is explicitly limited to an uncertain optimized processing window and allows that deviations may compromise performance, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis if any sample in a varied processing set fails. Failure of an off-window sample would not contradict the bounded hypothesis.
